name: AutoDS
tagline: Dropshipping automation: product research, bulk listing, price and stock monitoring, and automated order fulfillment across eBay, Shopify, Amazon, Facebook Marketplace and TikTok Shop.

pricing.basis: monthly, tiered by listing and order volume
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The visible product is a dashboard, and a dashboard is a weekend. Everything under it is not: authenticated write access to eBay, Shopify, Amazon and TikTok Shop listing APIs, scraped-and-normalized catalogs from dozens of suppliers, price and stock polling on hundreds of thousands of SKUs, and automated checkout on retail sites that actively fight automation. The product research numbers are aggregate sales data pulled from their own user base, which you cannot generate alone. You can absolutely build a personal price and stock watcher plus a listing CSV generator, and for a small catalog that covers most of the actual value. You cannot build the auto-ordering layer without becoming a bot maintenance company.
coreLoopDIY: Polls a list of supplier product URLs on a schedule, stores price and stock history in SQLite, alerts you when something moves, and exports marketplace-ready listing CSVs with your markup rules applied.
requirements: Node 20+ and a local machine or small VPS that can stay awake
Playwright with a headed or stealth browser profile for suppliers that block plain HTTP fetches
Per-supplier selectors or JSON endpoints you write and maintain yourself
A marketplace seller account if you want the CSV import path to actually work
Optional SMTP or Telegram token in .env for alerts
whatYouLose: Automated order placement: no bot places the supplier order and grabs the tracking number for you
Aggregate marketplace sales data, so product research goes back to guessing
Prebuilt supplier connectors that someone else fixes when a site changes its markup
Native marketplace API sync for inventory, orders and tracking uploads
Anti-block infrastructure: proxy pools, CAPTCHA handling, rate shaping across many suppliers
moatNotes: Auto-ordering is not a feature, it is an ongoing arms race against retailers who do not want you doing it. That maintenance burden is the product.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the alternative is a personal scraping fleet you babysit forever. Dropshippers pay for the fact that when Amazon changes a checkout flow or eBay rotates a listing field, someone else fixes it overnight and their store keeps running. The research data is a bonus, the fulfillment automation is the reason the subscription survives, and both scale in the vendor's favor as their user base grows. A DIY watcher is genuinely fine for ten products and quietly falls apart at two hundred.
notes: The dashboard is a weekend, the plumbing under it is a full-time job. The moat is maintained supplier connectors, marketplace API access, and aggregate sales data from a user base you do not have.
prompt:
Build a local dropshipping price and stock watcher. Single project, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable: TypeScript, Node 20, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Playwright for fetching, Fastify serving a plain server-rendered HTML UI with no frontend framework. No Docker.

Data model in SQLite:
- products: id, nickname, supplier_url, supplier_name, sku, selector_config JSON, markup_rule JSON, active
- snapshots: id, product_id, checked_at, price_cents, currency, in_stock, title, image_url, raw_error
- alerts: id, product_id, kind (price_up, price_down, out_of_stock, back_in_stock, fetch_failed), created_at, message, acknowledged

Features, in scope:
1. CLI command to add a product by URL. Store a per-supplier extraction config: either CSS selectors for price, title, stock, or a JSON-LD path. Ship configs for two example suppliers and make adding a third a config file edit, not a code change.
2. A poller that runs every product on an interval from .env (default 6 hours), writes a snapshot, and creates alerts on change using thresholds from .env.
3. Markup rules per product: fixed percent, fixed amount, or floor price. Compute a suggested sell price from the latest snapshot.
4. Web UI at localhost: table of products with current price, stock, 30 day sparkline drawn as inline SVG, suggested sell price, and an unacknowledged alerts panel.
5. Export a listings CSV with title, description stub, image URL, cost, suggested price, quantity. Generic columns only, do not pretend to match a specific marketplace importer schema.
6. Optional alert delivery via SMTP or Telegram, both read from .env, both disabled by default and silently skipped if unset.

Explicitly out of scope, do not build or stub: automated ordering on supplier sites, marketplace OAuth or API sync, proxy rotation, CAPTCHA solving, any product research or sales estimate feature.

Requirements: all secrets and tunables in .env with a committed .env.example. Retry fetches twice with backoff, record failures as alerts instead of crashing. Include seed data, a README with setup and a written warning that scraping selectors break and this needs manual upkeep, and vitest tests for markup math, change detection, and the JSON-LD extractor.
